transcript:
Header: Recorded 2026-09-29 15:00 PDT | Duration ~46m | Attendees: Jordan Park, Priya Singh (Redwood) - Alex Moreno, Dana Liu, Samir Patel (Maple Financial)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Park, AE at Redwood. Priya is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Alex (Maple Eng): Good, thanks. Ready to see the SDK walkthrough.
[00:11] Dana (DevOps): Hi all. We skimmed the docs but wanted a live run-through for env and auth.
[00:16] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, we'll cover Python and TypeScript quickstarts, show how to set the API key, env best practices, and a short demo hitting the hosted API. We'll also point out differences if you go Dedicated or Private.
[00:28] Samir (Security): Quick ask — we'll need to confirm KMS/HSM support and audit logging.
[00:33] Jordan: Yep, we'll cover high level; Priya will share the security pack after.

[02:05] Priya: Alright I'm sharing my screen — starting at the quickstart repo. The Python package name is redwood-inference (spoken), pip install redwood-inference or pip install redwood. In Node it's @redwood/inference via npm or yarn.
[02:28] Alex: And is the package the same for hosted and dedicated?
[02:34] Priya: Yes same SDK — you point the client at an endpoint or set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_BASE_URL for private. For hosted just REDWOOD_API_KEY is enough.

[04:12] Priya: Example Python snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate(prompt='summarize...') — that's the gist. In TS it's import { Client } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
[04:44] Dana: Are there helpers for streaming and chunking? We care about low tail latency.
[04:50] Priya: Yes we have streaming support in both SDKs, plus a streaming callback to handle tokens as they arrive. For latency controls you can set max_tokens_per_request, and for throughput use the Optimize dashboard to tune batching.

[06:10] Jordan: A common question — where to store keys. We recommend vault or cloud KMS. For Private deployments you can integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via BYOK and envelope encryption.
[06:30] Samir: Good. Can you send the exact flow for BYOK and audit logs?
[06:35] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll attach the security doc. Priya will include the KMS diagram.

[08:05] Priya: Now I'll run a quick TypeScript demo. Node app using the SDK — show me the sample route. (typescript code read out) 'app.post\('/generate'...)' — you can set up a route that proxies requests, use server-side environment var REDWOOD_API_KEY, don't ship keys in frontend.
[09:20] Alex: For our stack we use Next.js API routes — that'll work?
[09:27] Priya: Yep, Next API routes or serverless functions work fine. Just ensure the env var is on the server side.

[11:00] Dana: If we want private deployment in our AWS account, how does networking look? VPC peering, Transit Gateway?
[11:08] Priya: For Private we can support VPC endpoints, cross-account peering, or an on-prem appliance. We'll share the network playbook. There's also options for dedicated pods in your VPC.
[11:28] Dana: Ok we'll need that diagram.

[12:40] Priya: Quick note on configuration: client can accept model and generation params. Example 'client.generate({ model: "redwood-alpha-1", prompt, max_tokens: 256, temperature: 0.2 })'. Also mention quantized variants for dedicated to reduce GPU memory and cost.
[13:15] Jordan: Customers often ask about cost tradeoffs — hosted is easy and metered; Dedicated gives predictable latency and cost on committed capacity; Private for data residency/compliance.

[14:50] Samir: Does Redwood support SSO for team keys? We use SAML and SCIM.
[14:56] Jordan: Yes we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for console access; API keys lifecycle tied to user accounts or service principals. We'll include the enterprise auth flows in the pack.

[16:10] Priya: Now I'll switch to a live local run — I've got a small Python app that calls the SDK. I'm going to set ENV REDWOOD_API_KEY locally, then run 'python quickstart.py'.
[16:28] [screen shows terminal]
[16:34] Priya: You can see the request — we send the prompt, tokens come back streaming. Occasionally the transcript may show KV cache as 'KV cash' in auto-transcripts, lol — that's a common OCR issue.
[17:05] Alex: Ha. Can you show how to enable prefix caching?
[17:12] Priya: Prefix caching is configured on the server side and via flags in the client for cache keys. For hosted we manage cache transparently; for dedicated you can opt into caching TTLs. We'll share a config snippet.

[19:00] Jordan: On the Console side, quick overview — projects, routes, API keys, and the Optimize tab where we give batching and quantization suggestions. Priya, open the Optimize example.
[19:12] Priya: Sure. Optimize will suggest batch sizes based on your prompt length distribution, and recommend model variants with quantization. It also surfaces estimated cost savings and latency impact.
[20:30] Dana: Do suggestions translate to config we can apply automatically?
[20:36] Priya: You can export a policy or apply suggestions to a route; for Dedicated you might want to review before applying. We also support feature flags for canary testing.

[22:05] Alex: For the POC we want to run a small set of prompts against our dataset to verify quality and latency. What's the easiest way to do that?
[22:14] Priya: Send a sample prompt CSV or a notebook. We can run benchmarking tool that drives both hosted and dedicated endpoints and returns p95/p99 latency and token cost per response. We'll run with your timeouts and batching patterns.

[24:00] Jordan: I'll note that performance can vary by model family and sequence length; we'll baseline using your prompt set. Priya will coordinate.

[25:30] Samir: A security point — do logs contain PII by default? We need redaction options and retention controls.
[25:40] Priya: Logs can be configured; you can enable redact-on-ingest and set retention policies. For Private deployments logs stay in your account if you choose that path.

[27:05] Dana: Any gotchas for Dockerized deployments? Our app runs in k8s.
[27:12] Priya: Nothing special — install the SDK in your image, set env on the pod (k8s secrets recommended). For high throughput use connection pooling; Node SDK has keep-alive options. We'll include k8s sample manifests.

[29:00] Jordan: Quick pricing note — we'll send an estimate sheet. For Dedicated we often model committed vCPU/GPU hours and compare unit cost per million tokens.

[30:15] Priya: Back to code — small TS snippet for streaming: 'client.streamGenerate({ model, prompt }, onToken => { /* handle token */ })'. In practice attach to SSE or web socket handlers in your route.
[31:00] Alex: Does the SDK retry on transient errors?
[31:05] Priya: The SDK has built-in retry with exponential backoff and idempotency keys for generation requests. You can configure retry_count and backoff.

[32:40] Samir: For compliance, can we get SOC2/ISO artifacts and a BAA?
[32:48] Jordan: Yes SOC2 and ISO are available; BAA is available for healthcare customers — we'll confirm eligibility and send the docs.

[34:10] Dana: One operational question — is there a way to route certain customers or traffic to cheaper model variants automatically?

[34:22] Priya: Yes routing policies can send requests by route, region, and even by cost tier. You can set fallback models when capacity or cost thresholds are hit.

[35:50] Alex: Any sample app we can fork and run quickly?
[35:56] Jordan: We'll send the quickstart repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: placeholder) and include Python/TS examples and a small Next.js demo.

[37:20] Priya: I'll also attach the benchmark harness — CSV -> runner -> results dashboard. It's what we'll use for your prompt set.

[38:45] Samir: Timeline-wise we want a short POC in October, then decide for a pilot by November depending on results.

[39:10] Jordan: Sounds good. To recap: we demoed SDKs, auth, console, and Optimize. Jordan will send quickstart and pricing; Priya will run benchmarks; Samir/Dana will share infra and security docs.

[41:05] Alex: Thanks — that was helpful. One more small question: local dev flow — can devs use a scoped key with limited quota?
[41:12] Priya: Yes, create scoped API keys via the Console, with per-key rate limits and scopes. Great for dev vs prod separation.

[42:30] Jordan: Ok we'll follow up with the pack. Any final questions?
[42:37] Dana: None here.
[42:39] Samir: No. Thanks.
[42:42] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll send notes and next steps after this call.

[42:50] [call ends]

Notes: auto-transcription has minor errors (product names sometimes split, 'KV cache' -> 'KV cash', names occasionally misattributed). Shared artifacts referenced: quickstart repo (link), security pack (link), benchmark harness (link).
